title: Establishing Fungal Entomopathogens as Endophytes: Towards Endophytic Biological Control
protocol: Surface-sterilize bean seeds by immersing them in 0.5% sodium hypochlorite for two minutes.
Immerse surface-sterilized seeds in 70% ethanol for two minutes.
Rinse the seeds three times in sterile distilled water.
Plate 100 μl of the last rinsing water on PDA media and incubate at 25 °C for 10 days.
Terminate and restart the experiment if any growth is seen on the plate.
Plant sterilized seeds in groups of three in pots containing a sterile mixture of soil and sand at a 2:1 ratio.
Transfer the pots to a growth chamber with conditions set at 25 °C, approximately 50% RH, and a 12-hour photoperiod.
Eliminate the two least vigorous seedlings one week after germination.
Water every 2-3 days with sterile distilled water.
Fertilize plants with a 6 g/L water solution of NPK 15-15-15 fertilizer at 10 and 20 days after planting.
Obtain a commercial formulation of Beauveria bassiana strain GHA (Mycotrol SE).
Suspend one inoculating loop full of conidia in 1 ml of a 0.1% water solution of Triton-X 100.
Vortex the suspension for 10 seconds.
Plate 100 μl of the suspension on 2.5% Noble agar and incubate at 25 °C for 24 hours.
Transfer a single germinating conidium into a 100 mm plate containing PDA.
Grow until it covers the entire plate, typically taking 3-4 weeks.
Scrape fungal growth from the medium surface under sterile conditions.
Suspend scraped material in 10 ml sterile 0.1% Triton-X 100.
Vortex suspension for one minute.
Filter suspension through a sterile cheesecloth to remove hyphae and obtain stock suspension.
Estimate conidial concentration of the stock suspension using a hemocytometer.
Prepare a 10,000-fold serial dilution of the stock by transferring 100 μl of conidial suspension in 900 μl of 0.1% Triton-X 100 and vortexing for 10 seconds before each dilution.
Adjust the stock suspension to a final concentration of 10^8 conidia/ml using appropriate formula.
Plate 100 μl of the 10,000-fold dilution on 2.5% Noble agar.
Incubate plates at 25°C for 24 hours.
Inspect three random groups of 100 conidia to estimate percent germination.
Consider a conidium germinated when a visible germ tube longer than half the diameter projects from it.
Only use the suspension when the average percent germination exceeds 90%.
Water plants to soil capacity with sterile distilled water 24 hours before inoculation.
Use a manual atomizer to apply the conidial suspension or 0.1% Triton-X 100 to the adaxial surface of leaves until saturation is achieved.
Cover the top of the pot with aluminum foil to avoid runoff to the soil.
Cover plants with a plastic bag for 24 hours to maintain high humidity.
Use a graduated cylinder to apply 10 ml of conidial suspension or 0.1% Triton-X 100 to the surface of the soil at the base of the plant.
Return plants to growth chambers in a randomized complete block design, with no less than four additional experimental blocks installed for evaluations.
Evaluate each block randomly, selecting blocks in random order for large experiments that cannot be evaluated on a single day.
Measure and record the height from the base to the apical meristem before processing.
Uproot plants carefully and wash thoroughly in running tap water.
Sample two leaflets randomly from the first true leaf of each plant.
Obtain two stem samples, each 3 cm long, from the middle of the plant and near the soil surface.
Collect two taproot samples, each 3 cm long, from the middle of the root and from 1 cm behind the root tip.
Place the sampled leaflets, stems, and roots on three separate paper bags and label them appropriately.
Surface sterilize tissues in a sterile laminar flow hood.
Rinse each sample three times by immersion in sterile distilled water.
Dry each sample on sterile towel paper.
Dissect and discard the outer edges of each sample where endophytes might have been eliminated due to contact with disinfectants.
Cut the trimmed leaf samples into six sections, averaging 6x6 mm per section.
Cut the trimmed stem samples into six sections, each 6 mm long.
Cut the trimmed root samples into six sections, each 6 mm long.
Plate each of the six sections from a plant part on a 60 mm Petri plate with PDA media supplemented with tetracycline, streptomycin, and penicillin at 2 mg/L each.
Seal the Petri plates with parafilm.
Incubate the Petri plates in the dark at 25 °C.
Change the rinse water after processing each block of a given plant part.
Plate a 100 μl sample on PDA media.
Incubate the plate for 10 days at 25°C.
Inspect the plates every 2-3 days for 20 days to observe fungal growth.
Excise and transfer plant sections exhibiting presence of fungal endophytes to plates containing fresh PDA.
Record B. bassiana growth from plant sections.
Mount the specimen in a drop of water and inspect under a microscope when identification is uncertain.
Evaluate the impact of treatments on plant biomass using additional experimental blocks.
Measure height from base to top of apical meristem for each plant.
Carefully uproot and wash plants in tap water.
Dry plants at 45°C for three days to determine dry weight.
